title: Weight Reduction of the Overhead Stowage Compartment Installation — Request Held Pending Cabin Programme
abstract: Great Basin Airways asks for a lighter overhead stowage compartment installation to recover payload on thin long-haul sectors. The request is on hold pending the outcome of a wider cabin programme decision.

sections.request: On our thinner long-haul routes we are payload limited more often than we would like, and the cabin is where we think there is weight to be found. The overhead bins on our aircraft feel heavier than they need to be, particularly the latch and hinge hardware, and we would like to know whether a lighter installation is available or could be made available. We are not asking for larger bins and we do not want to change the cabin layout; we want the same volume for less mass. If there is a lighter latch assembly already in the catalogue we would take that on its own. We understand a lighter option may have been looked at before and dropped, and if that is the case we would like to know why so that we do not keep asking.
sections.background: Our network planning group estimates that eighty kilogrammes off the cabin would remove the payload restriction on two of our six long-haul city pairs in winter. We have already taken the lighter seat and galley options offered at delivery. We are aware that a lightweight latch change was studied and not carried through, and we have asked twice through our account team without a written answer.
sections.expected_outcome: A written position on whether a lighter overhead stowage installation is available for retrofit, and if not, a statement of what would be needed to make one available and on what timescale.

type_data.business_justification: A payload restriction on two winter long-haul city pairs, valued by the operator at roughly four hundred thousand euro a year in refused cargo.
type_data.closure_note: Held pending the cabin programme decision expected in the first quarter of 2027. A lightweight latch and hinge set was studied under an earlier modification and cancelled at design review because the flammability substantiation for a magnesium alloy inside the cabin needed a full-scale test campaign that was never funded, and because the corrosion case in the presence of galley spillage could not be closed with the proposed surface treatment. Reopening the request without a new material proposal would repeat that outcome, so the order stays on hold rather than being rejected outright. The operator has been given the written position it asked for and the file will be revisited when the cabin programme fixes its material policy.
